notes: Pages (column juan): Powell's book prints page N on PDF page N+6, the Economic Report of the President page N on PDF page N+8; the web pages and the CSV files have no pages. Disagreements between the sources: the official rate of 1949 was in effect from 19 September (Abbott, pw_abbott) or from 20 September 1949 (Powell, pw_dev49a and pw_sep20; the pound was devalued on 19 September, pw_fn75); in October 1950 the Canadian dollar rose 'five cents' to roughly US$0.95 (pw_oct2), from a par of US$0.9091 (pw_par49): about four cents; between 1952 and 1960 it traded between US$1.02 and US$1.06 (pw_premium), but the yearly lows of Historical Statistics of Canada are below US$1.02 in each year and below US$1.00 in 1952 and 1955 (hs560_1952, hs560_1955, hs560_1957, hs560_1959, hs560_1960; the snapshot canada_float_1946_1965); Coyne was Deputy Governor in January 1949 (Powell, pw_coyne49) or assistant to the Governor in 1944-1949 and Deputy Governor from 1950 (GND, gnd_coyne_bank); Obstfeld, Shambaugh and Taylor's text calls the Bretton Woods coefficient indistinguishable from zero (os_bwzero), their Table 1 marks -.20 and -.26 as significant at the 90 and 95 per cent levels (os_t1_bw). Second witnesses: Coyne's resignation on 13 July 1961 (Powell, pw_senate and pw_resigned: the day after 12 July; the Annual Report 1961, ar61_coyne); Rasminsky's appointment on 24 July (pw_rasminsky, ar61_coyne); the par value of 2 May 1962 (pw_may62, ar62_par, and 1/0.925 = 1.081); the US$1,050 million of June 1962 (pw_jun24, ar62_measures, ar62_credits), Powell citing the Annual Report 1962 (pw_ar62cite): one witness; the peak of US$1.0614 on 20 August 1957 (pw_premium) against the low of 0.9422 Canadian dollars per US dollar in 1957 (hs560_1957); Diefenbaker as Prime Minister (ar62_jun24, loc_diefenbaker_pm); Fleming's paper of November 1962 (bg_ref_fleming, fl_volume). Indirect testimony: the statements of Abbott (1950, 1951) and of Donald Fleming (1961, 1962), Coyne's memorandum of 1949 and his Annual Report for 1960, Friedman's debate of 1948, The Economist of 12 May 1962, Goforth (1950, pw_gravely), Muirhead (1999, pw_fn79b) and Helliwell, all through Powell; Donald Fleming's statement of 1 August 1961 as the Annual Report 1961 prints it (ar61_harmony); Rhomberg's econometric model through Fleming (fl_rhomberg) and Mundell (mu_rhomberg); Mundell (1961, 1973), McKinnon (1963) and Kenen (1969) through Mongelli (2002) and the Nobel press release; Mundell's paper of March 1962 through Powell (pw_fn82) and the Nobel press release (nb_assign). Single witnesses: the monetary policy of June-November 1962 (the interest-rate aim, the contraction of the money supply, the Bank Rate cuts of 12 October and 13 November: ar62_objective, ar62_rates, ar62_contraction, ar62_sept, ar62_cuts) rests on the Annual Report 1962 alone. Reading across a page: Powell's sentence 'Restrictive monetary policy ... led to a sharp deterioration in relations between the' (pw_restrictive) ends on the next page with 'Bank and the academic community.' (pw_restrictive2): the relations are those of the Bank with the economists, not with the government (pw_diefgov); the devaluation of 1949 'on' (pw_dev49a) ends on the next page with '20 September 1949.' and the call of footnote 75 (pw_sep20). Misreadings and misprints as printed in the quotations: 'Dornbuseh' for 'Dornbusch' (bg_dornbusch); 'Mundeil' for 'Mundell' (bg_before); 'Mundelfs' for 'Mundell's' (bg_vernacular); Powell prints 'Milton's Friedman's' (pw_friedman3); the text layer letter-spaces 'recommended more vigorous foreign exchange' (pw_imfstaff); 'cross-border' with the Unicode hyphen U+2010 (ry_certainly). Not obtained: Mundell (1961) and McKinnon (1963) in the American Economic Review (JSTOR answered with a bot check, not passed); Kenen (1969); Friedman (1953); McKinnon (2004); Mundell (1962), IMF Staff Papers; Rey's Jackson Hole paper of 2013 (the NBER version says it was presented at the Jackson Hole Symposium, without a year: ry_jh); the IMF's Annual Reports of 1950 and 1962 (imf.org refused access); the House of Commons Debates (no terms of use found for the site, not quoted); the Bank of Russia's table of its refinancing rate (the rate rises of May 1998 rest on Chiodo and Owyang alone). The volume of McKinnon (1963) in Mongelli's references (mg_ref_mckinnon) is not checked. Life dates: Donald Fleming, Diefenbaker and Friedman from the Library of Congress; Abbott, Coyne and McKinnon from the GND (the LoC heading of Coyne has no year of death: loc_coyne); Marcus Fleming, Kenen and Mundell from both; Rasminsky: the LoC heading gives 1908 and no year of death (loc_rasminsky), no record in the GND or data.bnf.fr: '生卒年未详'. Rows of other snapshots used by the chapter: intro_facts (co_band, co_gko30, co_twice, co_depleted, co_aug17, co_sep2), external_facts (lk_adjust, lk_float), brettonwoods_facts (bo_pegged, b59_conv, b61_reval, b70_de_inflow, b70_de_float, bt_de_c, b70_fr_flight, bo_controls_de) and bis_fx (lkr_usd_eop, February and April 2022).
